BLOCKER: Language-rule violation: `core/execution_trail.py` adds new shipped logic (`TEST_KINDS`, `test_kind`, `tests_by_kind`) in Python; the rule requires new shipped logic in Go, yet AC claims language-rule checks pass.

`gate2_completion_check.check()` semantics silently changed: `continue` moved inside the new `if gaps:` block, so `GATE0_INCOMPLETE` no longer short-circuits and gap-present ids skip all remaining gate diagnostics (masking other problems).

No producer for `DISPOSITION_APPROVAL` decisions appears in the diff, while `record_gate_decision` explicitly refuses anything except APPROVE/APPROVE_WITH_ATTENTION; if no other path exists, ACCEPTED/DEFERRED approvals can never be recorded and the whole policy is unsatisfiable.
MAJOR: `finalize_item.build()` hardcodes `item_revision = revision + 1` and Gate 2 requires exact match; any extra revision bump during `backlog.update` (or any later edit, e.g. a gate decision recorded after finalize) makes the report permanently stale — an undocumented ordering/feedback-loop hazard with no regeneration guidance.

AC completeness is only "list non-empty": nothing cross-checks `ac_verification` against the item's authoritative AC list, so all-but-one-AC recorded still passes Gate 2/completion despite the "any AC is missing" AC.

Enforcement drift: `execution_trail_check` checks only final_report *presence* + ACs, while `completion_gaps` also checks `FINAL_REPORT_STALE`; two different notions of "complete" can disagree between CI and merge gate.
Duplicated deferred-follow-up logic (`FOLLOW_UP` regex, external-id + existence checks) in both `disposition_policy.py` and `execution_trail_check.py` — divergence risk on the same policy rule.

No test covers the actual persistence path (`backlog.update` with `final_report`), `record_gate_decision` refusals, or Gate 2 refusal — AC demands tests for final-report persist and completion guards.
Confirm `usage_totals` output actually carries `cost_source` and extracted deferred backlog `id`s; the AC requires both explicitly and the diff never adds/verifies them.
MINOR: `test_kind` classification is precedence-brittle heuristic (`"conformance"` → logic wins over db/api; `"db_"`/`" db"` substring matches) — a single command string can flip category over time.
`from core import backlog as _backlog` is imported inside the per-item loop in `execution_trail_check.evaluate`.
Disposition policy in `record_gate_decision` is applied to `mode = "design" if gate == 1 else "diff"`, silently mapping gate 1.5/completion to "diff" without documenting the mapping.
`review-dispositions.json` booleans are re-read per call with no schema/validation and defaults duplicated in code (`STATUSES`, cap parsing).

AC says Gate 2 "refuses" on bad ACs, but refusal lives in `record_gate_decision` only; a direct `check()` run reports `AC_VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE` without blocking the decision path if that path is bypassed.
NIT: Unrelated `config/id-blocks.json` session allocation hunk bundled into this change.
Inconsistent `str(x or "").upper()` vs `str(x).upper()` result parsing across `finalize_item`, `gate_decisions`, and `execution_trail_check`.
Show's "Tests by kind" ratio omits skipped counts while the table includes them.
SUMMARY: Solid structure (config-driven policy, persisted report, show rendering, guard tests), but a language-rule violation on new Python shipped logic and the re-indented `continue` in the Gate 2 completion check are merge-blocking.
Biggest long-term risks: unsatisfiable/incomplete DISPOSITION_APPROVAL production path, revision-coupled staleness feedback loop, and divergent completeness checks between CI and the merge gate.
